page_title: Let's build a URL shortener in Go - Part II : Storage Layer

summary.title: Let's build a URL shortener in Go - Part II : Storage Layer
summary.one_liner: You learn how to set up a Redis-backed storage layer in Go for a URL shortener, with unit and integration tests using testify.
keywords: building a link shortener in go part 2
redis as cache for hot values
go project directory structure store package
how to unit test redis storage in go
takeaways: The storage layer is set up as a store package with a wrapper around the Redis client.
Storage APIs for persisting and retrieving URL mappings are designed and implemented on top of Redis.
Unit and integration tests are written for store initialization and storage APIs using the testify library.
In production, Redis holds hot, frequently requested values while an RDBMS such as Postgres or MySQL stores cold data.
summary.summary: This is Part II of a series on building a URL shortener and forwarder in Go backed by Redis. It walks through creating a store package with store_service.go and store_service_test.go, wrapping the Redis client, and designing the storage API that persists and retrieves URL mappings. The part ends with installing github.com/stretchr/testify and writing unit and integration tests for store initialization and the storage APIs. The page is light on code, so details of the implementation are not shown in the text.
